name: libslax
desc: Implementation of the SLAX language (an XSLT alternative)
why: An obscure SLAX language implementation offering an XSLT alternative, a strange corner of the language world.

brief.what_it_is: libslax is an open-source C library and command-line toolset that implements SLAX, an alternative syntax for XSLT that follows the look of C and Perl. It takes SLAX source files (.slax) and runs or converts them, and it can emit XML, JSON, or YAML. The installed executables are slaxproc (the SLAX processor), gt (a git-style helper that appears to be the project's own development workflow tool), and slax-config. It is built on top of libxml2 and libxslt.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki pitches SLAX for readability: 'If you like: if ($this == that) { expr the/other; } else { expr "neither"; } more than: <xsl:choose>... please consider using SLAX.' The README credits libxml2 and libxslt as the foundation the library builds on.
brief.how_it_works: SLAX is parsed into the same model XSLT uses, so libslax leans on libxslt for execution. The release notes show a formatter (--width, line wrapping), a profiler (--profile, --profile-mode), and a --dump-tree option that prints a script's hierarchy. Scripts can also be converted to and from XML with xutil:slax-to-xml() and xutil:xml-to-slax(). The README itself says little about internals, so this is taken from the release notes.

brief.install_notes: Build from source is documented: the build uses autoreconf, and the 0.23.0 notes mention --with-sqlite3[=DIR] as an optional configure switch and a SH_OPTS debugging hook. libxml2 and libxslt are required dependencies; readline or libedit is used for the interactive shell unless disabled with +slaxIoUseReadline or --no-readline. The brew caveats field is empty. The README does not describe first-run steps or configuration.
brief.standout: A pretty-printed syntax for XSLT, in a corner of the language world that few people use, maintained by one author (Phil Shafer) and shipped with its own tooling. The release notes reference a 'version 1.3' of the language with optional parentheses, a JSON and YAML output mode, and a built-in profiler.
brief.status: Maintained, based on the GitHub releases page. The latest release is libslax-3.1.6 (dated 26 Aug, with the year not shown in the fetched text), and the prior release, 3.1.5, is dated 13 Aug. The commit notes reference compatibility work for libxml2 2.15.2 and bison 3.8.2. By contrast, the wiki home page was last edited on Aug 20, 2013 and its news items date from 2013, so the wiki is stale.
brief.caveats: The wiki is largely a 2013 snapshot from the move off Google Code, and its build-status badges are empty. The README is very short and mostly points to the wiki and to libslax.readthedocs.io. The license is referenced only as a 'Copyright' file and the Juniper terms are not quoted in the text I read, so check the repository for the actual license. The README also includes a Google Analytics snippet. Documentation and examples are not in the README and I did not follow the readthedocs link.
quotes: SLAX is an alternative syntax for XSLT which is tailored for readability and familiarity, following the style of C and Perl.
